title: HeyClicky vision note (Farza)
text:
﻿My name is Farza.


I will spare you a cringe manifesto. The facts:


I am going all-in on building a new interface for computers.


My first major swing is heyclicky, a simple AI buddy that lives on your Mac.


It is a wonderful form factor and starting point. The product is literally 5-weeks old, and in that short time it has become extremely powerful. We’re at 250,000 messages sent, 50,000 agents spawned, 3500 WAUs, and 185 paying customers.


These numbers aren’t massive, but, they are not small either.


It’s very early and hacky, but, I think the current version of of the product is a glimpse into the future we’re heading towards where the models will be the primary way we interact with our computer.


And that’s the vision I want to build this company around, with a focus on consumers.


When I was 12 years old, my father bought the iMac for us. It changed my world!


I had a computer before called an Acer T180. But, the iMac just made everything so simple.


All of a sudden I was learning video editing, making friends on the internet, and starting my first business. The iMac just made it all so accessible for me. I think we are in a similar spot with AI where a tiny tiny % of humanity actually understands how to utilize it’s power.


Tech Twitter does not reflect the real world.


In reality, no one knows this technology can do real work for you. The 14 year old in Lagos doesn't know this thing can build the game living in his head. The mom in Islamabad running a Shopify store doesn’t know it can handle orders while she sleeps. The nurse in Florida doesn't know it can see her screen and teach her anything she wants in real-time.


We all have access to same models yet very few of us actually unlock them!


And, I just believe it’s an interface problem.


The iMac took the same chip, memory, and storage everyone else was using and made it 100x more accessible. I wanna take the same frontier models everyone else is using, and make it so that the power of this technology can break out of uninspired chat interfaces or clunky terminals and into the hands of that next curious 12 year-old or professional. 


Much of this is early and exploratory. I don’t want the above to come off as “my big vision”. After all, this is only 5-weeks old and main goal right now is to keep shipping and keep learning. But, I believe there’s something here and the early pull we have is a good signal.


Today, we’re seeing everyone from business customers to solo entrepreneurs to kids use heyclicky. The use cases are vast.


Right now, it’s just me.


I'm assembling a small full-time team to build this with me. Maybe 6 to 10 people max. I'm less interested in what you call yourself and more in what you can make.


I’m looking for people who love building products to help me on the engineering front (plz, I suck), people constantly tinkering with the latest models to help me push the product in wild new ways, people who love media and filmmaking to help me tell the story of this thing across the internet, people who love socials and growth to help me blow up even more, people who are wonderful designers to help crack a new interface that the next billion people will use.


Your background doesn’t matter to me.


I don’t care if you are broke film student who works at Starbucks or an OpenAI researcher getting paid a milli by Papa Sam. Please just tell me about yourself, show me stuff you’ve done, tell me what you want to do here and your ideas, where you’re based, and your timelines.


If you are legit and your work speaks for itself, great, show me. I wanna work with the best.


If you are younger, and don’t have a whole lot, that’s fine. Do not send me your resume. If you wanna do design here, show me a design for heyclicky. If you wanna be a filmmaker here, great, record a video for the product and show me. If you wanna be an engineer here take this repo, remix it, and demo your ideas.


In 2026, I index 100X more on ideas than skill. Skill can be gained, great ideas are rare.


No remote. I’m happy to help you relocate to SF if you’re in another city. I’m sorry, but can’t help directly with visas right now unless your situation is relatively simple (ex. TN visa). This administration sucks and getting work visas is near impossible unless you have a really high-tier background. 


We’d work together for 30-45 days part-time or full-time to see if there’s synergy, and go from there!


If interested, let me know!


hi@heyclicky.com


You can also DM me on Twitter but please note I get insane traffic there sadly and have a tough time keeping track.


If you are talented as fuck and have been looking for an opportunity to make stuff alongside a group of other people driven to build something wonderful and have fun doing it, please reach out. This may finally be it.


- Farza
